subject: FastCart renewal: throughput bridge & prorated rate structure
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@fastcart.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <procurement@fastcart.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastCart renewal: throughput bridge & prorated rate structure

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the initial renewal sync last week. Per our conversation I put together a recommended renewal that balances predictable unit economics with room for FastCart's seasonal peaks. High-level: 3x monthly commit (hosted API) versus current 1.2x, a 10% volume discount on the new tiers, and a 20% burst pocket for peak season that is billed at a reduced overage rate. I've attached the proposal (FastCart_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf).

Key asks / notes for your team:
- Confirm target effective date: Oct 1, 2027 (we can prorate September usage).
- Confirm expected Q4 spike window and whether a larger temporary burst is needed.
- If procurement needs alternate billing terms (net30 vs net45) flag Lina and me.

Operational protections included:
- Soft-throttle thresholds that maintain latency SLOs for critical endpoints.
- Canary rollout for any model/throughput changes with automatic fallback to current capacity.

If that looks reasonable I'll loop in Karthik and Kimberly to finalize the term sheet and pricing. Open to a quick call tomorrow if you want to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@fastcart.com>

Cc: Lina Gomez <procurement@fastcart.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastCart renewal: throughput bridge & prorated rate structure

Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear proposal. A few items from our side:

1) The 3x monthly commit gets us where we need to be for baseline Q4 load, but we have a marketing-led flash sale expected Nov 12–14 that could spike traffic ~6–7x baseline for a 72-hour window. Can we add a temporary spike allowance that won't immediately trigger standard overage rates?

2) Pricing: the 10% volume discount is helpful, but procurement is requesting either a deeper discount on committed tokens above 5T tokens/month or a blended rate for the burst pocket. Lina, can you confirm preferred invoicing cadence (we typically do net45)?

3) Can you confirm whether the soft-throttle will prioritize our core checkout and personalization endpoints first? Latency there is critical.

If you can send a version that reflects a prorated start (Sept 15 effective for billing) and a separate line item for a temporary spike buffer (Nov flash sale), we can fast-track to legal.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Engineering | FastCart
sanjay@fastcart.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: FastCart renewal: throughput bridge & prorated rate structure

Folks —

Forwarding Sanjay's reply. TL;DR: they want a temporary spike allowance for Nov flash sale (6–7x for ~72 hours), request net45, and want prioritization for checkout endpoints. Proposed internal approach:

- Offer a one-time Nov spike buffer equal to 4x their monthly commit for a 72-hour window, priced at 50% of our standard overage rate (blended burst rate). This keeps them covered without a huge one-off bill.
- Keep the 3x monthly commit baseline; for >5T tokens/month we can add a stepped discount (15% on incremental tokens above 5T).
- Confirm soft-throttle endpoint prioritization: we should include a technical appendix in term sheet that documents endpoint tagging and SLA routing during throttle events.
- Prorated start: propose Sep 15 effective (bill Sep 15–30 pro rata), with Oct 1 full month.

Questions for pricing/legal ops:
- Kimberly: are you comfortable with 50% of overage as the burst blended rate for that temporary buffer?
- Karthik: any constraints on canary rollout / routing that would affect our ability to guarantee endpoint prioritization?

I can draft the term sheet (v2) with those edits and send back to Sanjay + procurement — if you approve, I'll include the technical appendix and DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Marissa

Sanjay / Lina —

Thanks for the rapid feedback. Attached is the revised term sheet (FC_Renewal_TermSheet_v3.pdf) and a short usage projection (usage-projection.csv) that shows the expected baseline and the modeled Nov flash sale. Summary of changes: 

- Baseline commit: 3x current monthly (committed tokens line item) effective Sep 15, 2027 (prorated Sep 15–30).
- Burst buffer: one-time Nov buffer equal to 4x monthly commit for the Nov 12–14 window, billed at 50% of standard overage (single line item, clearly labeled).
- Stepped discount: 15% discount on incremental tokens above 5T/month.
- Billing terms: net45 as requested (invoice to procurement@fastcart.com).
- Operational protections: soft-throttle that prioritizes checkout and personalization endpoints; technical appendix included showing endpoint tagging + canary routing.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the revised term sheet so I can send a DocuSign envelope (link included in the related_links entry).
2) Once signed we will schedule a brief ops runbook call (30 min) to cover endpoint tagging and the canary plan for the Oct ramp and the Nov flash.

If we get sign-off today we can have the DocuSign routed and into legal by tomorrow end-of-day.

Cheers,
Marissa
